body.statement: If probability laws on a separable metric space converge weakly, then random elements with those laws and the limiting law can be constructed on one probability space so that the random elements converge almost surely.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 1.10.3 (a.s. representations). Let X_alpha:Omega_alpha -> D be D_alpha-measurable maps. If X_alpha converges weakly to X_infinity and X_infinity is separable, then there exist D_alpha-measurable maps X_tilde_alpha:Omega_tilde -> D defined on some probability space (Omega_tilde,A_tilde,P_tilde) with, eventually: (i) X_tilde_alpha converges almost uniformly to X_tilde_infinity; (ii) X_tilde_alpha and X_alpha are equal in law on D_alpha for every alpha.

attestation.note: Direct transcription in ASCII notation from van der Vaart and Wellner (1996), Theorem 1.10.3, p. 58, in the National Academic Digital Library of Ethiopia public repository scan at https://ndl.ethernet.edu.et/handle/123456789/26495. The core uses the separable-metric sequential specialization. DOI metadata: https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4757-2545-2.
